A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MCTS-based data construction and CoT-aware post-training work. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. Both contain 11 pages, end with references, and contain no appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original SFT and DPO experiments, reasoning-length analyses, joint-loss comparisons, and MCTS inference results in Tables 3–7.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds SFT comparisons for three additional student-model configurations in Table 4.

M1.justification: The MCTS procedure, thought nodes, model coordination, length balancing, cDPO, prefix masking, and joint objective remain unchanged. Section 3.1 clarifies relative path lengths within each query; v1 already described ranking responses to the same question by length.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GSM8K, MATH/MATH500, AIME 2023–2024, Blocksworld, and eight-language Multi-IF. The additional student models use retained tasks. Translation and multimodal reasoning appear only as future directions in v2.

E2.justification: Table 4 retains the comparison between the instruction-tuned starting model, Sky-T1-based SFT, and SFT with the authors' data, repeating it on additional backbones. No competing training method is added or removed, and the comparator sets in Tables 5–7 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 4 substantially broadens SFT validation from Llama-3.1-8B alone to include Llama-3.2-1B and Qwen2.5-7B/1.5B, extending evaluation across model families and much smaller student sizes. The retained benchmark definitions, post-training sequence, joint-loss settings, and Test@1/8/32 protocol are unchanged.

E4.justification: The error cases, CoT-length analysis, cumulative post-training ablations, joint-loss weight sweep, and MCTS inference exploration retain the same evidence. Table 4 extends the main SFT comparison to additional model configurations without introducing a separate ablation or diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The parenthetical percentages in Tables 5–6 remain no-answer rates, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds substantial results across student families and scales. For example, v2 newly reports Llama-3.2-1B GSM8K scores of 50.0 with the authors' data, 43.4 without additional SFT, and 37.2 with Sky-T1. Both newly tested 1B/1.5B students remain at 0.0 on AIME. All retained result entries and plotted findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The UCB expression, cDPO loss, joint training objective, and mathematical definitions are unchanged. The added arithmetic-versus-integral example illustrates relative reasoning lengths without introducing a derivation or formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution bullets retain the claims about distillation difficulties, constructing CoT trees from scratch, and complementary CoT-aware optimization. The additional experiments support existing claims, while the shortened conclusion preserves their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 removes the Limitations section acknowledging increasing MCTS computational expense and discussing pruning and specialized-model rotations. It adds an explanation connecting relative CoT length to problem complexity and shifts future-work discussion toward translation, multilingual, and multimodal reasoning.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-homepage link and explicitly explains per-query length selection without fixed token thresholds. Removing the Ethics Statement also removes the statement that all datasets are publicly available; this does not establish an actual change in resource availability.

R1.justification: The conclusion adds references to Liu et al. (2025) on translation, Zeng et al. (2025) on multilingual instruction following, and Li et al. (2025b) on multimodal reasoning. Existing research positioning remains substantially unchanged; shortened author lists do not represent removed works.

P1.justification: v2 adds the Marco-o1 v2 title prefix, revises author/contact information, expands Section 3.1, edits the data-validation description, and condenses the conclusion. Limitations and Ethics Statement sections disappear, but the main section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 4 expands from one backbone block to four. Tables 3, 6, and 7 move between columns, and surrounding text reflows. All four figures remain unchanged, with no broader visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The expanded Table 4 provides useful evidence that the constructed SFT data transfers beyond one 8B backbone to another model family and much smaller students. Clearer length-selection documentation and the project link also help. Removing the computational-cost limitation weakens transparency, and the full post-training method still lacks broader-model validation, so the net improvement is limited.
